newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St Barbara withdraws Leyshon bid.
newsitem.headline: St Barbara withdraws Leyshon bid.

text.p: Gold miner St Barbara Mines Ltd said on Tuesday that it has withdrawn its takeover offer for Mt Leyshon Gold Mines Ltd.
St Barbara told the Australian Stock Exchange that it had secured the required consent from corporate watchdog, the Australian Securities Commission, to withdraw the bid.
Mt Leyshon earlier this month recommended shareholders not accept the St Barbara offer, saying a takeover did not produce a clear advantage for shareholders.

St Barbara said last Wednesday that Normandy Mining Ltd, the largest shareholder in Mt Leyshon, had advised it would follow the Mt Leyshon board's recommendation and not accept the offer for its stake of about 75 percent.

St Barbara's offer of 32 of its shares for every 10 Mt Leyshon shares would have given Normandy a 41.3 percent stake in the merged group, which would have had annual gold output of about 350,000 ounces.
Mt Leyshon initially said it was receptive to the bid, given that its Mt Leyshon gold mine in Queensland had a limited life.

However, Mt Leyshon directors said later that while St Barbara's exploration tenements near Meekatharra in Western Australia were prospective, the recent history of mining in the area was typified by low-grade, medium to high cost operations.
Mt Leyshon shares last traded at A$1.91 on Monday while St Barbara shares closed one cent down at A$0.64 on Tuesday.
